Horrific
Sep 2026 • Solo
Absolutely appalling treatment over a pair of shoes.

We arrived at MILA tonight for a reservation we had been looking forward to, only to be turned away because my pregnant friend was wearing the suede sandals pictured in this review.

To be completely transparent, MILA’s reservation notes do state “no flip-flops.” These were elevated suede sandals worn with a long dress—not rubber beach or pool flip-flops. MILA is certainly entitled to enforce its dress code. What was unacceptable was the way we were treated while they did it.

The person at the entrance was incredibly rude and dismissive. When I explained that my friend was pregnant and had chosen comfortable footwear for that reason, I was actually told that I should have noted her pregnancy on our reservation and that doing so “would have been helpful.”

I genuinely cannot understand why a woman should be expected to disclose that she is pregnant when making a dinner reservation—or why that information should be necessary for a restaurant to treat her with basic courtesy and use reasonable discretion over a pair of suede sandals.

There was no gracious explanation or attempt to help us find a solution. We were simply made to feel unwelcome and turned away. You can enforce a dress code without humiliating your guests, and a restaurant positioning itself as a luxury hospitality experience should understand that distinction.

We left and happily spent our money elsewhere. Miami has far too many excellent restaurants that understand hospitality for us to ever return to MILA.

I’m including a photo of the shoes that resulted in us being turned away so prospective guests can see exactly what MILA considers unacceptable footwear—and pregnant guests may apparently want to make a note of their pregnancy when booking.

MILA trades heavily on sensuality and sophistication, but that sex appeal quickly cools when the fundamentals suggest a lack of refinement or knowledge. The food itself, however, was excellent.
